page: Microsoft Azure FX64-16mds_v2 is a constrained-core virtual machine configuration within the memory-intensive FXmdsv2 family, hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. The server features 16 vCPUs (8 physical cores with 2 threads per core) allocated from an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache, along with vector and matrix extensions including AVX-512 and AMX instructions. A notable architectural characteristic is the extreme memory density, provisioning 1344.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 84.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided through a 3780 GB NVMe SSD. No dedicated GPUs are included.

Benchmark measurements highlight strong single-threaded capabilities driven by high clock speeds and architectural features. The Geekbench single-core score of 2353.0 and text processing score of 2923.0 both reach top-tier percentiles. Single-threaded compression pipelines perform favorably, evidenced by a 34.06 GB/sec gzip compression score and 14.78 GB/sec bzip3 decompression score in the top quartile. Large-block uncached memory write bandwidth also demonstrates strong throughput at 91.75 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics remain moderate due to the 16-vCPU cap, with multi-core Geekbench (13593.0) and PassMark CPU (29623.8) remaining in the middle tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX64-16mds_v2 minimizes per-core software licensing costs while retaining the memory capacity and high clock speeds of larger host machines. The inclusion of bundled NVMe storage and vast memory capacity makes it well suited for memory-bound relational databases, large in-memory caches such as Redis, and high-frequency analytical processing where per-core licensing expenses dictate limiting active compute cores.
description: Microsoft Azure FX64-16mds_v2 is a specialized virtual machine designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, the instance provides 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) alongside an expansive 1344.0 GB of memory, equating to 84.0 GB per vCPU. Compute features include a 260 MB L3 cache, AVX-512, and AMX support. Fast ephemeral storage is bundled via a 3780 GB NVMe SSD, while no GPUs are attached. High clock speeds deliver top-tier single-core performance, reflected in elevated Geekbench single-core scores and rapid compression rates. With uncached memory write bandwidth reaching 91.75 GB/sec and average Redis throughput at 24.29 million ops/sec, this instance offers exceptional density for per-core licensed databases, large in-memory key-value stores, and data-heavy analytics requiring massive RAM footprints.
